newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK FARMERS THREATEN TO REPEAT ROAD BLOCKADES.
newsitem.headline: GREEK FARMERS THREATEN TO REPEAT ROAD BLOCKADES.

text.p: Greek farmers threatend on Thursday to repeat crippling road blockades that had cut the country in two last month if their demands are not satisfied by February 4.
"We are warning the government 20 days ahead of time in order to avoid bringing tractors out in the streets," farmers' representative Yannis Patakis told televesion.

A 25-day blockade in December paralysed road traffic and left thousands of trucks stranded along Greek highways. The farmers suspended their action during the holidays but vowed to repeat it if demands were not met.
Demands include lower fuel costs and Value Added Tax (VAT) on farm equipment, higher price supports, especially for cotton and a $1.3 billion rescheduling of debts to the state Agricultural Bank.
Farmers in central Greece will launch as of January 28 a series of protests, mostly disrupting public services, ahead of a full-scale blockade to warn the government they mean business, Patakis said.
"We will block civil services, tax offices and toll booths in our area to prevent the state from collecting money," he said. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 MES/DRK
